args.body:
DEVIATION-AND-EXPOSURE ANNEX
Northgale Systems, Inc. / Corvid Analytics LLC — Master Services Agreement
Corvid rev B counter-draft (9 July 2026) vs. Northgale client form v2 (execution-ready base)
Prepared for the Northgale negotiation file — Deal Committee consideration (meeting 4 August 2026)

Exposure convention. Per the Northgale GC engagement instruction of 14 July 2026 and the 2026 Commercial Contracting Playbook drafting note, all dollar exposure below is computed at the stated monthly run-rate of $85,000 per month (MSA §4.1 Base Fee). No amount is invented; every figure derives solely from figures stated in the client form v2, the Corvid rev B markup, the 2026 playbook, and the engagement instruction letter.

PLAYBOOK POSITION KEY
Standard = playbook standard position; Fallback = Approved fallback (concedable without escalation); Escalation = requires the stated approver.
PB-1 Renewal: Standard 1-yr; Fallback NONE; multi-year renewal requires CLO approval.
PB-2 Convenience: Standard 30 days; Fallback up to 45 days; above 45 days requires CLO approval.
PB-3 Wind-down: 30-day cap; out-of-pocket + non-cancelable third-party costs only; full-fee wind-down is out of policy.
PB-4 Payment: net 30; late interest never above 1.0%/mo; suspension out of policy unless ≥30 days' cure notice + CFO sign-off.
PB-5 Limitation of liability: Standard 24-month cap; Fallback floor 18-month; a 12-month period is below the floor and requires CLO approval; deletion of any carve-out requires joint CLO + CFO approval.
PB-6 Service credits: Standard 20% cap; Fallback floor 15%; a 10% cap is out of policy.

EXPOSURE COMPUTATIONS (at $85,000/month)

A. Limitation-of-liability cap ($85,000 × measurement months):
   - Client form / playbook Standard (24 months): 24 × $85,000 = $2,040,000
   - Corvid rev B proposed (12 months): 12 × $85,000 = $1,020,000
   - Playbook Approved fallback floor (18 months): 18 × $85,000 = $1,530,000
   Note: rev B's 12-month period is below the playbook fallback floor of 18 months and requires CLO approval. Moving from the standard 24-month cap to rev B's 12-month cap would reduce aggregate exposure by $1,020,000 ($2,040,000 − $1,020,000); holding at the 18-month fallback floor would hold exposure at $1,530,000.

B. Maximum monthly service credit (credit cap as % of $85,000 monthly fee):
   - Client form cap (20%): 0.20 × $85,000 = $17,000/month
   - Corvid rev B cap (10%): 0.10 × $85,000 = $8,500/month
   - Playbook Approved fallback floor (15%): 0.15 × $85,000 = $12,750/month
   Note: rev B's 10% cap is below the fallback floor and is out of policy. Moving from the client-form 20% cap to rev B's 10% cap reduces Northgale's maximum monthly credit from $17,000 to $8,500; the playbook floor of 15% would preserve a $12,750 monthly cap.

C. Wind-down compensation (full-fee vs. out-of-pocket):
   - Corvid rev B §7.4: 60-day full-fee wind-down = 2 months × $85,000 = $170,000 full-fee compensation for the wind-down period, plus all committed third-party costs (additional, uncapped).
   - Playbook PB-3: wind-down capped at 30 days and compensated at documented out-of-pocket costs and non-cancelable third-party commitments only (no full fee) — full-fee wind-down is out of policy.
   Note: The proposed full-fee wind-down carries a $170,000 full-fee cost that the playbook does not permit; under the playbook the wind-down yields no full-fee component and only documented out-of-pocket/third-party costs. The full-fee wind-down also breaches PB-3's 30-day cap (rev B proposes 60 days).

ITEMIZED DEVIATIONS — REV B CHANGE-BY-CHANGE

Change 1 — Section 2.2 (Renewal): 1-year → 2-year renewal periods.
   - Client form: automatic renewal in successive one (1) year periods.
   - Markup (rev B): successive two (2) year periods (capacity planning rationale).
   - Playbook (PB-1): Standard 1-year; Fallback NONE (multi-year renewal periods of any length are out of policy); any multi-year renewal requires Chief Legal Officer (CLO) approval.
   - Dollar impact: none directly quantifiable from the documents at the stated monthly fee; exposure arises structurally (multi-year lock-in without a playbook-approved fallback). Escalation required: CLO.

Change 2 — Section 4.3 (Late Amounts): interest 1.0% → 1.5% per month.
   - Client form: 1.0% per month on late undisputed amounts (no right to suspend for non-payment).
   - Markup (rev B): 1.5% per month.
   - Playbook (PB-4): late interest never above 1.0% per month.
   - Dollar impact: rev B's 1.5% exceeds the playbook's 1.0% ceiling; 50 basis points of incremental monthly interest on any late amount. Specific dollar exposure depends on the amount in arrears, which is not stated in the documents; escalation of the incremental rate above the 1.0% ceiling.

Change 3 — NEW Section 4.4 (Suspension of Services).
   - Client form: no suspension right (grants Provider no right to suspend Services for non-payment).
   - Markup (rev B): Provider may suspend Services if an undisputed invoice remains unpaid fifteen (15) days after its due date.
   - Playbook (PB-4): suspension-of-services rights are out of policy unless preceded by at least thirty (30) days' written cure notice, and any suspension right requires CFO sign-off.
   - Dollar impact: no dollar figure is assigned in the documents; operational/continuity risk from a 15-day cure (below the 30-day cure the playbook requires). Escalation required: CFO sign-off.

Change 4 — Section 7.2 (Termination for convenience): 30-day → 90-day notice.
   - Client form: 30 days' prior written notice; no wind-down period or compensation.
   - Markup (rev B): 90 days' prior written notice.
   - Playbook (PB-2): Standard 30 days; Approved fallback up to 45 days; any notice period above 45 days requires CLO approval.
   - Dollar impact: rev B's 90-day notice extends the notice run rate by 60 days over the standard 30 days, or by 45 days over the 45-day fallback, during which the $85,000 monthly fee continues — i.e., up to 2 additional months (≈$170,000) vs. the standard, or 1.5 months (≈$127,500) vs. the 45-day fallback. Specific dollar exposure depends on whether termination is exercised; escalation required (CLO) for any period above 45 days.

Change 5 — NEW Section 7.4 (Wind-Down): 60-day full-fee wind-down.
   - Client form: no wind-down period and no wind-down compensation.
   - Markup (rev B): 60-day wind-down during which Customer pays the full monthly base service fee plus all committed third-party costs (for any termination other than Provider's uncured material breach).
   - Playbook (PB-3): acceptable only if capped at 30 days and compensated at documented out-of-pocket costs and non-cancelable third-party commitments only; full-fee wind-down is out of policy.
   - Dollar impact: full-fee wind-down = 2 months × $85,000 = $170,000 full-fee compensation + uncapped third-party costs, versus the playbook's out-of-pocket-only position which carries no full-fee component. Also breaches PB-3's 30-day cap (60 vs. 30 days). Out of policy.

Change 6 — Section 9.1 (Limitation of Liability): 24-month → 12-month cap.
   - Client form: cap measured at Fees paid/payable in the 24 months preceding the first event giving rise to liability.
   - Markup (rev B): 12 months.
   - Playbook (PB-5): Standard 24-month; Approved fallback floor 18-month; a 12-month period is below the fallback floor and requires CLO approval.
   - Dollar impact: 24-month cap = $2,040,000; 12-month cap = $1,020,000; 18-month fallback floor = $1,530,000 (all at $85,000/month). rev B's proposal would reduce the cap by $1,020,000 vs. the standard; the fallback floor would hold it at $1,530,000. Escalation required: CLO.

Change 7 — Section 9.2 (Carve-Outs): deletion of clause (c) (gross negligence / willful misconduct).
   - Client form: carve-outs from the §9.1 cap for (a) Confidentiality, (b) IP Indemnification, and (c) gross negligence or willful misconduct.
   - Markup (rev B): deletes clause (c), subjecting gross negligence and willful misconduct to the §9.1 cap; retains (a) and (b).
   - Playbook (PB-5): the carve-outs for confidentiality, IP indemnification, and gross negligence/willful misconduct are non-negotiable; deletion of any carve-out requires joint CLO and CFO approval.
   - Dollar impact: capping gross negligence/willful misconduct at the (rev B) 12-month value of $1,020,000 would cap liability that the client form leaves uncapped. No independent dollar figure is stated; escalation required: joint CLO + CFO.

Change 8 — Section 11.2 (Service Credits): aggregate cap 20% → 10%.
   - Client form: aggregate service-credit cap of 20% of the monthly base fee per month.
   - Markup (rev B): aggregate cap of 10%.
   - Playbook (PB-6): Standard 20%; Approved fallback floor 15%; a 10% cap is out of policy.
   - Dollar impact: client-form cap = $17,000/month; rev B cap = $8,500/month; playbook fallback floor = $12,750/month. rev B's 10% cap cuts the maximum monthly credit by $8,500/month vs. the standard and is out of policy; the 15% floor would preserve $12,750.

SUMMARY OF OUT-OF-POLICY ASKS (escalation items)
- Change 1 (2-yr renewal): multi-year renewal — CLO approval.
- Change 2 (1.5% late interest): above the 1.0% ceiling — escalation.
- Change 3 (suspension, 15-day cure): below the 30-day cure and lacks CFO sign-off — CFO.
- Change 4 (90-day convenience notice): above the 45-day fallback — CLO.
- Change 5 (60-day full-fee wind-down): full-fee and 60-day, both out of policy — policy breach.
- Change 6 (12-month cap): below the 18-month fallback floor — CLO.
- Change 7 (carve-out deletion): non-negotiable carve-out deletion — joint CLO + CFO.
- Change 8 (10% credit cap): below the 15% fallback floor, out of policy — policy breach.

Prepared for the Northgale negotiation file. All values computed solely from figures stated in the underlying documents; no amounts have been invented.
